# Relivaro CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run build` from src/cli/commands.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Version 1.5.0. All commands accept `--json` (machine-readable output on stdout, errors as JSON on stderr), `--quiet`, `--no-color` and `--help`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success (no gate failed) |
| 1 | A gate failed: findings at/above `--fail-on`, release not ready, breaking API change, fix verification failed, rollback conflict |
| 2 | Usage or configuration error, missing permission flag (`--allow-exec`, `--yes`), refused target |
| 3 | Unexpected runtime error |
| 4 | Partial run: a limit (`--max-duration`, `--max-files`, `--max-bytes`) or SIGTERM/SIGINT stopped it early; the record is written with `partial` |

## `relivaro audit`

Complete engineering audit (security, supply chain, reliability, performance, quality, testing).

```
relivaro audit [path] [options]
```

Runs every rule category. With --allow-exec it also runs the project's type check and tests; with --online it checks dependencies against OSV.dev.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--category <list>` | Restrict to categories: security, supply-chain, reliability, performance, quality, testing, release. |
| `--online` | Query OSV.dev for known dependency vulnerabilities (sends package names and versions only). |
| `--allow-exec` | Allow running project commands (tests, build, type check, lint). They execute project code. |
| `--format <list>` | Report formats to write: json, md, html, sarif. Default: `json,md,html`. |
| `--out <dir>` | Also copy the reports to this directory. |
| `--fail-on <severity>` | Exit with code 1 when an open finding (medium/high confidence) is at or above this severity. |
| `--rule <ids>` | Only run these rules (prefix with * suffix allowed, e.g. "sec/*"). |
| `--config <file>` | Path to relivaro.config.json. |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Where run data is stored (default: <project>/.relivaro). Use it to keep the analysed repository untouched. |
| `--baseline <file>` | Baseline file (default: relivaro-baseline.json if present). |
| `--no-baseline` | Ignore any baseline file. |
| `--no-git` | Do not use git to list files (walk the tree instead). |
| `--since <git-ref>` | Show only findings on lines changed since this git ref (plus untracked files); the whole tree is still analysed. |
| `--osv-cache <file>` | OSV cache file to use (shared between runs; a read-only file is used without being written). |
| `--osv-api <url>` | HTTPS mirror of the OSV API, used with --online. |
| `--offline-osv` | Look up known vulnerabilities in the OSV cache only (no network); uncached packages are unverified. |
| `--root-label <name>` | Show this name instead of the absolute project path in every report, message and snippet. |
| `--snippet-lines <n>` | Source lines per finding snippet (default 3); 0 is the same as --no-snippets. |
| `--no-snippets` | Leave source snippets out of every report. |
| `--max-duration <seconds>` | Stop the analysis after this many seconds; the run is partial (exit code 4). |
| `--max-files <n>` | Analyse at most this many files (root manifests and lockfiles first); partial beyond it. |
| `--max-bytes <size>` | Analyse at most this many bytes of files (K, M or G suffix); partial beyond it. |
| `--no-gitignore` | Without git, also analyse files matched by .gitignore (they are counted and named otherwise). |
| `--assume-tracked` | Without git (archives, exports), treat every file as committed so sensitive files such as .env are reported (by path, never read). |
| `--no-inline-suppressions` | Ignore relivaro-ignore/relivaro-accept comments in the audited code (for code you do not trust). |
| `--no-write` | Do not write run data or reports (stdout only). |
| `--max-findings <n>` | Findings printed to the terminal. Default: `15`. |
| `--compact` | With --json: summary, open findings without rule boilerplate, checks, test gaps, release and limitations (for agents). |
| `--open` | Open the HTML report with the default application. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro audit
relivaro audit ../my-app --online --format sarif --out reports
relivaro audit . --allow-exec --fail-on high
```

## `relivaro fix`

Plan, apply, verify and roll back deterministic fixes.

```
relivaro fix <list|plan|show|apply|rollback|history> [args] [options]
```

```
Subcommands:
  list [path]                 Fixable findings in the project
  plan [path]                 Generate a fix plan with diffs (no files are changed)
  show [plan-id|latest]       Print a plan and its diffs
  apply [plan-id|latest]      Apply a plan (requires --yes); verifies first
  rollback [apply-id|latest]  Restore files from the backup of an applied fix
  history                     List applied fixes

Apply verifies every change statically (the targeted findings disappear and no new findings appear) and,
with --verify "<command>" --allow-exec, runs the command in an isolated copy of the project before and
after the change. The working tree is modified only if verification passes. Rollback refuses to overwrite
files edited after the fix unless --force is given.
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--finding <ids>` | plan/apply: only these finding ids. |
| `--rule <ids>` | plan: only findings of these rules. |
| `--fixer <ids>` | plan: only these fixers. |
| `--include-review` | plan: include fixers that intentionally change behaviour (marked "review"). |
| `--online` | plan: allow fixers that need the network (gha-pin-action resolves tags to commit SHAs from the action's GitHub repository). |
| `--yes` | apply: confirm modifying the working tree. |
| `--verify <command>` | apply: command that must pass after the fix (e.g. "npm test"). |
| `--allow-exec` | apply: allow running the verification command. |
| `--no-isolate` | apply: run verification in the working tree (auto-rollback on failure) instead of a temporary copy. |
| `--force` | rollback: restore backups even if files changed after the fix. |
| `--path <dir>` | Project directory for show/apply/rollback/history (default: .). |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro fix plan
relivaro fix show latest
relivaro fix apply latest --yes --verify "npm test" --allow-exec
relivaro fix rollback latest
```

## `relivaro report`

Re-render a stored run in other formats.

```
relivaro report [run-id|latest] [--path <project>] [--format md,html,sarif,json] [--out dir]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--path <dir>` | Project directory (default: .). |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |
| `--format <list>` | Formats to write. Default: `md,html`. |
| `--out <dir>` | Output directory. |
| `--open` | Open the HTML report with the default application. |

## `relivaro compare`

Compare two runs: introduced, resolved and persisting findings, check regressions.

```
relivaro compare [base=previous] [head=latest] [--path <project>] [--fail-on <severity>]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--path <dir>` | Project directory (default: .). |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |
| `--fail-on <severity>` | Exit 1 if an introduced finding is at or above this severity, or a check regressed. Default: `none`. |

## `relivaro review`

Record verified verdicts (confirmed, false positive, needs runtime, accepted risk) for findings of a run.

```
relivaro review <add|list> [--finding <ids>] [--verdict <v>] [--reason <text>] [options]
```

```
Subcommands:
  add    Record a verdict for one or more findings of a run (one justification for all of them)
  list   Show the recorded verdicts of a run

Verdicts are stored in runs/<run>/review.json next to the run and never change the original findings.
Reports re-render with the reviewed state: raw detection and reviewed conclusion side by side. Record only
what was actually checked in the code; unreviewed findings stay "detected".
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--finding <ids>` | add: finding id(s) of the run. |
| `--verdict <verdict>` | add: confirmed, false-positive, needs-runtime or accepted (an explicitly accepted risk). |
| `--reason <text>` | add: short justification (required). |
| `--evidence <file:line>` | add: code locations that support the verdict (project-relative). |
| `--severity <severity>` | add: severity the reviewer considers appropriate, if different. |
| `--reviewer <name>` | add: who reviewed (e.g. "claude-code", a person's handle). Default: agent. |
| `--human` | add: the reviewer is a person, not an AI agent. |
| `--run <id>` | Run id or alias. Default: `latest`. |
| `--path <dir>` | Project directory (default: .). |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro review add --finding RLV-3f9a1c2b --verdict confirmed --reason "user input reaches the query" --evidence src/db.ts:42
relivaro review add --finding RLV-1,RLV-2 --verdict false-positive --reason "test fixture, never deployed"
relivaro review list --json
```

## `relivaro recheck`

Re-check findings of an earlier run against the current source before repairing them.

```
relivaro recheck [path] --finding <ids> [--run <id>]
```

Re-runs only the rules behind the given findings and reports each one as present (same place), moved (same code, other line) or gone (fixed, or the code changed). Use it before editing code for findings taken from a report or a prompt.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--finding <ids>` | Finding ids from the run (required). |
| `--run <id>` | Run the ids came from. Default: `latest`. |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro recheck . --finding RLV-3f9a1c2b,RLV-7fb00c34 --run 20261101-120000-abc123
```

## `relivaro baseline`

Accept current findings as a baseline so only new findings fail gates.

```
relivaro baseline [path] [--reason <text>] [--from <run-id>]
```

Writes relivaro-baseline.json (fingerprints only, no code or secrets) to the project root. Commit it to share the baseline. Baseline findings remain visible in reports.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--reason <text>` | Justification stored with every entry. |
| `--from <run>` | Use findings of this stored run instead of running a new audit. |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |
| `--output <file>` | Baseline file path (default: <path>/relivaro-baseline.json). |

## `relivaro bench`

Benchmark a command repeatedly and compare with a saved baseline.

```
relivaro bench --cmd "<command>" [--name build] [--runs 10] [--warmup 1] [--save-baseline] --allow-exec
```

Measures wall-clock time of a project command (no shell) over several runs and reports mean, median, p95 and standard deviation. Results are stored in .relivaro/bench/<name>/ and compared against baseline.json with a significance check. Use performance.budgets in the config to make `relivaro release` enforce limits.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--cmd <command>` | Command to measure (required). |
| `--name <name>` | Benchmark name (default: derived from the command). |
| `--runs <n>` | Measured runs. Default: `10`. |
| `--warmup <n>` | Unmeasured warm-up runs. Default: `1`. |
| `--save-baseline` | Store this result as the new baseline. |
| `--allow-exec` | Required: the command runs project code. |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro bench --cmd "npm run build" --name build --runs 5 --allow-exec --save-baseline
relivaro bench --cmd "npm run build" --name build --runs 5 --allow-exec
```

## `relivaro load`

Controlled HTTP load test against a local or private-network service.

```
relivaro load <url> [--duration 10] [--concurrency 10] [--method GET] [--header "K: V"] [--body <json>] [--name api]
```

Sends requests with bounded concurrency for a fixed duration and reports throughput, latency percentiles, status codes and error rate. Targets must resolve to loopback/private addresses (public hosts are refused unless --allow-remote, and hard caps always apply: 64 concurrent, 120 s, 200k requests). Never point this at production.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--duration <sec>` | Test duration in seconds. Default: `10`. |
| `--concurrency <n>` | Concurrent connections. Default: `10`. |
| `--requests <n>` | Stop after this many requests. |
| `--method <method>` | HTTP method. Default: `GET`. |
| `--header <"K: V">` | Request header (repeatable; commas are not split for this option). |
| `--body <text>` | Request body. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | Per-request timeout. Default: `10000`. |
| `--name <name>` | Result name for baselines/budgets. |
| `--save-baseline` | Store this result as the new baseline. |
| `--allow-remote` | Allow non-private targets you are authorized to test (caps still apply). |
| `--path <dir>` | Project directory for storing results (default: .). |
| `--workspace <dir>` | Workspace directory. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro load http://localhost:3000/api/health --duration 15 --concurrency 20 --name health
```

## `relivaro contract`

Validate OpenAPI specs and detect breaking API changes.

```
relivaro contract <validate|diff> <spec> [other-spec] [--base <git-ref>]
```

```
validate <spec>: structural checks (versions, unresolved $refs, undeclared path parameters, duplicate operationIds, undefined security schemes).
diff <old> <new> | diff <spec> --base <git-ref>: classifies changes as breaking or compatible (removed endpoints/responses, new required parameters, type changes, removed response properties, narrowed enums).
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--base <git-ref>` | diff: compare <spec> with its version at this git ref. |

Examples:

```bash
relivaro contract validate openapi.yaml
relivaro contract diff openapi.yaml --base origin/main
```

## `relivaro rules`

List rules or show one rule in detail.

```
relivaro rules [list|show <id>] [--category <c>]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--category <list>` | Restrict to categories: security, supply-chain, reliability, performance, quality, testing, release. |

## `relivaro init`

Create relivaro.config.json (and optionally a GitHub Actions workflow).

```
relivaro init [path] [--github-action] [--force]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--github-action` | Also write .github/workflows/relivaro.yml (SARIF upload to code scanning). |
| `--force` | Overwrite existing files. |

## `relivaro doctor`

Check that Relivaro and optional toolchains work in this environment.

```
relivaro doctor
```

## Global options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print machine-readable JSON to stdout (errors as JSON on stderr). |
| `--quiet` | Only print the essential result (no progress). |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output (also honours NO_COLOR). |
| `--lockdown` | Hosted scanning of untrusted code (also RELIVARO_LOCKDOWN=1): no processes, no network, no writes into the audited tree, no repository config or inline suppressions, no git. |
| `--ignore-repo-config` | Ignore the audited repository's relivaro.config.json; use defaults or --config. |
| `--progress` | Progress on stderr: tty, plain (also RELIVARO_PROGRESS=1), ndjson (one JSON event per line, also with --json) or off. |
| `--help` | Show help for the command. |
